manager_rule: Resolve the Rule-52 vs Rule-34 compiler-suppression conflict in round R+2. When BOTH of the following are simultaneously active in a round designated R_2 by the Rule-52 protocol: (A) Rule 52 has stored a non-empty deferred_rule46_bypass_nets (e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}) awaiting bypass application in round R_2, AND (B) Rule 51 mandates mandatory_kelvin_bypass in round R_2 for cable C_asym's single-member Kelvin force stub injection, which per Rule 34 suppresses ALL compiler stubs: (1) override the mandatory_kelvin_bypass compiler suppression ONLY for nets whose names are members of deferred_rule46_bypass_nets — compiler stubs for those specific nets are passed through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination, honoring Rule 52's deferred bypass intent; (2) compiler stubs for ALL other nets (not in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets) remain suppressed per Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass protocol as normal; (3) the cable C_asym Kelvin force stub is still injected with full absorber-exempt mandatory_kelvin_bypass status as Rule 51 mandates — this part of Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass behavior is not overridden; (4) log 'rule52_rule34_partial_override_applied' with fields: (a) round R_2, (b) cable C_asym and the injected force stub coordinates, (c) nets in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets that received the partial override with confirmation absorber bypass was honored for each, (d) confirmation all other compiler stubs were suppressed per Rule 34, (e) DRC and kelvin_unrouted from round R_2; (5) clear deferred_rule46_bypass_nets to empty immediately after round R_2 is dispatched regardless of outcome, per Rule 52's existing reset protocol. This rule is additive to Rules 34, 46, 51, and 52; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate beyond the specific compiler-suppression override described here. Rationale: Rule 52 was authored to defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round when Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass suppression would otherwise void it in R+1 — but Rule 52 did not account for Rule 51 also imposing mandatory_kelvin_bypass in R+2 (for cable C_asym). Rule 34's 'suppress ALL compiler stubs' clause applies in R+2 by default, silently voiding Rule 52's deferred bypass for deferred_rule46_bypass_nets in exactly the round it was meant to fire. Without an explicit precedence rule, both Rules 51 and 52 are technically honored in spirit but their effects are contradictory in execution: Rule 52's bypass-deferral mechanism becomes inoperative whenever it lands on a mandatory_kelvin_bypass round, wasting both the Rule-46 false-positive detection and the Rule-52 deferral. The partial override preserves Rule 34's primary intent (Kelvin injection priority; all other compiler stubs suppressed) while rescuing Rule 52's bypass for the specific nets it identified, preventing the deferral mechanism from silently failing.
